# pretest 1.0.1

First working install path. `install.sh` in 1.0.0 aborted on its own checksum
step: the checksum file names `pretest.py` while the installed file is `pretest`,
so `sha256sum -c` could not find it. The installer now compares the two hashes
directly. `pretest.py` is otherwise unchanged.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/alexwest1981/pretest/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
```

Installs to `~/.local/bin/pretest`. Or take the file itself:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/alexwest1981/pretest/releases/latest/download/pretest.py -o pretest
chmod +x pretest
curl -fsSL https://github.com/alexwest1981/pretest/releases/latest/download/pretest.py.sha256 | sha256sum -c -
```

## Use

```bash
pretest --url https://example.com
pretest --url https://example.com --domain example.com --repo ~/code/app
pretest --url https://app.example.com -H "Cookie: session=…"   # behind a login
pretest --url https://example.com --fail-on high               # CI gate
pretest --self-test                                            # verify the tool
```

Exposed artefacts, transport and TLS, header hygiene, cookie flags, CORS,
SPF/DMARC/DKIM/CAA, subdomains via crt.sh with dangling-CNAME takeover detection,
20 common ports, secrets in source, and dependency CVEs through `npm audit` /
`pip-audit` / `cargo audit` when installed.

Anything it could not check is reported as `info` — it never goes quiet.

## Limits

Not a pentest: no IDOR, no business logic, no injections in your own parameters.
Report text is Swedish, every finding has a stable English `id` in the JSON.
TLS 1.0/1.1 show as *untested* on a modern OpenSSL, not as unsupported. Port
findings behind a CDN describe the CDN edge and say so. Windows is untested.

## Verification

CI at this tag: `self-test (3.10)`, `(3.12)`, `(3.13)`, `(3.14)` all green.
